logs.label: Logs
logs.description: Logs important server actions, tracks invites and adds the /clear command.

clear.description: Quickly delete messages in the current channel.

opt.count: Number of messages to delete (1 to 100).
opt.member: Only delete messages from one member.

clear.invalidChannel: ❌ This command must be used in a server text channel.
clear.botNoPerm: ❌ I do not have the “Manage Messages” permission in this channel.
clear.failed: ❌ Could not delete these messages. Check my permissions.

rollback.missing: ❌ This rollback cannot be found or has expired.
rollback.notAllowed: ⛔ You are not allowed to use this rollback.
rollback.unsupported: ❌ This rollback type is not supported.
rollback.noPermission: ❌ I do not have the required permissions to restore this item.
rollback.failed: ❌ Could not restore this item. Check my permissions and hierarchy.

invitations.description: See who invited whom on this server.

opt.member: One member’s tally instead of the leaderboard.

invitations.disabled: ❌ Invite tracking is disabled on this server.

logChannelId.label: Log channel
logChannelId.help: Where the server's logs are published.

messages.label: Log messages
messages.help: Logs deleted and edited messages: author, channel, old and new text. A deletion comes with a button that reposts the message. Needs the privileged « Message Content » intent: without it the entry is still written, but the text is missing.

members.label: Log members (joins/leaves)
members.help: Logs joins and leaves, with the account's age — the first sign of a wave of fake accounts. The bot cannot tell someone leaving from someone being removed; removals are covered by the moderation category instead.

channels.label: Log channels
channels.help: Logs channels created, deleted and renamed, along with their permission changes. A deletion comes with a button that recreates the channel with its settings — but not its messages, which Discord does not give back.

roles.label: Log roles
roles.help: Logs roles created, deleted and changed — name, colour, and above all permissions. This is the category that shows a role just gained « Administrator », which otherwise only gets noticed after the damage.

moderation.label: Log moderation
moderation.help: Logs sanctions: timeouts, bans, kicks, voice disconnects and mutes, with who issued them and why. The issuer is read from Discord's audit log, so the bot needs the « View Audit Log » permission — without it the sanction is logged without saying who took it.

invites.label: Track invites (who invited whom)
invites.help: Ties each arrival to the invite that brought it and feeds /invites. Requires the “Manage Server” permission.
